analysis.investment_thesis: Data Patterns is one of the finest defense electronics businesses I have encountered in India — 43% operating margins, zero debt, 31% revenue CAGR, and a genuine moat built on security clearances, DRDO relationships, and deep technical expertise in radar, EW, and avionics. Unfortunately, at 79x PE, 60x EV/EBITDA, and P/S of 20x, the market has already priced in a decade of flawless execution, and a great business at a terrible price is still a poor investment.
key_strengths: Exceptional 43% operating margins and 53% gross margins — pricing power characteristic of a near-monopoly supplier to Indian defense
Pristine balance sheet: zero debt (D/E 0.00), growing equity from INR 575 Cr to INR 1,508 Cr in three years
Structural tailwind from India's Atmanirbhar Bharat defense indigenisation drive — import substitution creates a multi-decade runway
key_risks: Extreme valuation at 79x PE and 60x EV/EBITDA — any growth disappointment or contract delay will be punished severely
Negative free cash flow (-INR 196 Cr in FY25) despite strong reported profits — defense contracts create brutal working capital cycles
Customer concentration: government/defense procurement is lumpy, bureaucratic, and subject to budget prioritisation risk
red_flags: OCF was negative in both FY23 (-INR 17 Cr) and FY25 (-INR 90 Cr) — only 2 of 4 years produced positive operating cash; profits are accrual, not cash
P/S ratio of 20x on INR 708 Cr revenue against INR 19,562 Cr market cap — even if revenue doubles, the stock remains extremely expensive
At the current price, the company would need to sustain 30%+ growth for 10+ years with margin expansion just to justify today's valuation — any slippage makes the investment poor
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Data Patterns is a genuinely exceptional franchise. The combination of 43% operating margins, zero debt, 31% three-year revenue CAGR, and high entry barriers from security clearances and certified technical expertise represents the kind of business I would love to own for 20 years. Promoter holding of 42% at the IPO and growing equity base show a management team that thinks like owners. The Atmanirbhar Bharat tailwind is structural, not cyclical.

But price matters enormously, and this price is extreme. At 79x trailing PE, the market is not just pricing in the next few years of growth — it is capitalising the next decade into today's share price. The negative FCF in FY25 (-INR 196 Cr) is a reminder that defense contractors carry enormous working capital burdens between contract award and payment. I have seen many fine businesses destroy investor returns because the entry price left no margin of safety. I admire this company unreservedly and would buy it at 30–35x earnings.
